cards.b: Close together in a regular pattern; particles only vibrate about fixed positions.
Close together but irregular; particles slide past each other.
Far apart, random arrangement; particles move quickly in all directions.

cards.f: Which states have a fixed volume?
cards.b: Solids and liquids. Gases have no fixed shape or volume and are easily compressed.

cards.f: Why can gases be compressed but liquids cannot?
cards.b: Gas particles are far apart with lots of space; liquid particles are already touching.

cards.f: Why does a gas's volume increase when heated (at constant pressure)?
cards.b: Particles gain kinetic energy, move faster and hit the walls harder and more often, so the gas expands.

cards.f: Why does gas pressure rise when volume is decreased (constant temperature)?
cards.b: Particles are closer together so they collide with the walls more frequently.
Net movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to lower concentration, due to random motion.

cards.f: Which gas diffuses faster: NH₃ or HCl? Why?
cards.b: NH₃: lower relative molecular mass (17 vs 36.5), so lighter particles move faster.

cards.f: Flat part of a heating curve: what is happening?
cards.b: A change of state; energy is used to overcome forces between particles, so temperature stays constant.
Element: one type of atom. Compound: different elements chemically bonded. Mixture: substances not chemically joined.

cards.f: Relative charge and mass: proton, neutron, electron
cards.b: Proton +1, mass 1. Neutron 0, mass 1. Electron −1, mass 1/1840 (negligible).
Proton number = number of protons. Nucleon (mass) number = protons + neutrons.
Atoms of the same element with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.

cards.f: Why do isotopes have the same chemical properties?
cards.b: Same number of electrons, so the same electronic configuration (neutrons do not affect chemistry).

short.q: Describe how the particles are arranged and move in a liquid. [2]
short.model: Particles are close together in an irregular arrangement and can slide past one another.

short.q: Explain, using kinetic particle theory, why increasing the temperature of a gas in a sealed syringe increases its volume if the pressure is constant. [3]
short.model: Particles gain kinetic energy and move faster, hitting the walls harder and more often, so the volume must increase to keep pressure constant.
points: collide with walls more often and with greater force

short.q: Sodium ion ²³₁₁Na⁺: state the number of protons, neutrons and electrons. [3]
Cotton wool soaked in ammonia and one in hydrochloric acid are placed at opposite ends of a glass tube. A white ring forms nearer the HCl end. Explain. [3]
short.model: NH₃ has a lower Mr than HCl so its particles diffuse faster and travel further, meeting HCl nearer the HCl end.
points: diffuses faster so ring forms nearer HCl

short.q: Chlorine has two isotopes, ³⁵Cl and ³⁷Cl. State two similarities and one difference. [3]
short.model: Same number of protons and electrons (same chemical properties); they differ in the number of neutrons (18 and 20).
points: same number of electrons/same electronic configuration
